name: Paterius notarius Gregorii I
modernTranslations: Unknown. Paterius was a compiler of Gregory I's biblical exegesis (Liber testimoniorum veteris testamenti); modern translation status unclear.
untranslatedHighlights: Liber testimoniorum veteris testamenti (entire work).

name: Wernerus S. Blasii
modernTranslations: Unknown. Author of Liber deflorationum (medieval biblical commentary); no English translation located.
untranslatedHighlights: Liber deflorationum (entire surviving work).

name: Angelomus Luxovensis
modernTranslations: None located. Works include Commentary on Genesis, Enarrationes In Libros Regum, Enarrationes In Cantica Canticorum.
untranslatedHighlights: Commentarius in Genesin; Enarrationes In Libros Regum; Enarrationes In Cantica Canticorum (all biblical commentaries).

name: Eugenius III
pdTranslations: Scattered individual letters exist in public domain sources (e.g., letter to King Louis VII, 1145).
modernTranslations: Individual letters translated in scholarly collections on the Second Crusade; no complete edition.
untranslatedHighlights: Most papal correspondence remains in Latin.

name: Symphosius Amalarius
modernTranslations: Eric Knibbs's complete English translation of the Liber officialis (De ecclesiasticis officiis) published as 'On the Liturgy' (Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library, Harvard University Press, 2014).
untranslatedHighlights: None; major work fully translated.

name: Petrus Pictaviensis
pdTranslations: Compendium appears in English in Matthew Parker's early vernacular Bibles (London, 1568+); text is heavily interpolated and liberally translated from Latin.
modernTranslations: No comprehensive modern English translations located.
untranslatedHighlights: Summa de confessione; most theological works remain in Latin.

name: Eusebius Vercellensis
modernTranslations: No modern English translations documented. Jerome attributed to him a Latin translation of Eusebius of Caesarea's Psalms commentary and other translations, but these are lost.
untranslatedHighlights: Nearly all attributed works lost or survive only in fragments.

name: Maximus Taurinensis
modernTranslations: Boniface Ramsey, OP, translated complete sermons for Ancient Christian Writers series, vol. 50 (Newman Press, 1989). Based on Almut Mutzenbecher's critical Latin edition.
untranslatedHighlights: None; major homiletic corpus fully translated.

name: Innocentius II
pdTranslations: Scattered individual letters, chiefly public-domain translations of papal correspondence.
modernTranslations: Letters to Heloise and other scattered correspondence available in Epistolae database (Columbia University); no comprehensive modern edition.
untranslatedHighlights: Bulk of papal letters remain in Latin (Migne P.L. CLXXIX).

name: Prosper Aquitanus
modernTranslations: P. De Letter, S.J., translated Defense of Augustine (Ancient Christian Writers 32, 1963) and Call of All Nations (ACW 14, 1952). Epitoma Chronicon available in A. C. Murray's 'From Roman to Merovingian Gaul: A Reader' (2003). Other works may remain untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: De gratia Dei et libero arbitrio and some other treatises status unclear.

name: Bruno Herbipolensis
modernTranslations: No English translation located. Psalterium (commentary on Psalms with appended analysis of biblical hymns from Church Fathers) exists in Patrologia Latina only.
untranslatedHighlights: Psalterium beati Brunonis episcopi herbipolensis (entire work).

name: Sicardus Cremonensis
modernTranslations: No English translation documented. Mitrale (de officiis ecclesiasticis summa) in 9 books exists in critical Latin editions (Sarbak & Weinrich, 2008; Migne, 1855).
untranslatedHighlights: Mitrale, sive De officiis ecclesiasticis summa (comprehensive liturgical treatise, 9 books).

name: Gilbertus Foliot
modernTranslations: No comprehensive English translation. Critical Latin edition: The Letters and Charters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Dom Adrian Morey and C. N. L. Brooke (Cambridge University Press, 1967). Individual letters may appear in scholarly articles.
untranslatedHighlights: Letters and Charters (bulk of surviving work).

name: Radulfus Ardens
modernTranslations: Christopher P. Evans edited and translated 'The Questions on the Sacraments' from Speculum universale 8.31–92 (Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies, Toronto, 2010; Brepols). Broader Speculum universale remains unexplored and largely untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Summa de vitiis et virtutibus / Speculum universale (14 volumes; only sacramental sections translated).

name: Prudentius Trecensis
modernTranslations: Unknown. Medieval theologian (distinct from the poet Prudentius). Known for De praedestinatione contra Joannem Scotum. No English translation found.
untranslatedHighlights: De praedestinatione contra Joannem Scotum (entire work).

name: Ekkehardus Uraugiensis
modernTranslations: No English translation located. German translation by Pflüger (Leipzig, 1893). Latin texts in MGH and Patrologia Latina.
untranslatedHighlights: Chronicon universale (world chronicle with German history 1098–1125).

name: Burchardus Wormaciensis
modernTranslations: Preface translated by R. Somerville and B. Brasington in 'Prefaces to Canon Law Books in Latin Christianity: Select Translations 500–1245' (Yale, 1998). Only a few penitential questions translated.
untranslatedHighlights: Decretum (complete penitential manual/canon law compilation).

name: Eadmerus Cantuariensis
modernTranslations: Life of Anselm (Vita Anselmi) translated. Historia novorum in Anglia likely remains in Latin. Lives of Saints manuscripts circulated widely but remain largely untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Historia novorum in Anglia (1066–1122); Lives of Saints (Oda, Dunstan, Oswald, et al.).

name: Ambrosiaster
modernTranslations: Gerald L. Bray, Ancient Christian Texts series: Commentaries on Romans and 1–2 Corinthians (first complete English translation of these commentaries). Additional commentaries (Galatians–Philemon) also in ACT series. Other works may remain untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Status of remaining biblical commentaries beyond Romans, Corinthians, Galatians–Philemon unclear; may be partially or fully translated.

name: Lactantius
pdTranslations: William Fletcher translation in Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 7 (1886); fully public domain. Available free at CCEL, New Advent, Internet Archive.
modernTranslations: Anthony Bowen and Peter Garnsey, Translated Texts for Historians series, vol. 40 (Liverpool University Press, 2003). Catholic University of America Press edition also available.
untranslatedHighlights: None; major works (Divine Institutes, Anger of God, etc.) fully translated.
